eventMetadata.context_description: Current Met Office forecasts for London on May 17 point to a daily maximum near 17°C, with an approaching Atlantic front bringing increasing cloud cover and scattered light showers that will limit afternoon insolation and cap peak heating. Mid-May climatology at Heathrow places the long-term average high at 16–17°C, so traders’ near-even distribution across the 15°C, 16°C, and 17°C contracts reflects uncertainty over exactly how much the frontal cloud deck will suppress temperatures below the seasonal baseline. Model ensembles remain tightly clustered around these values, with only modest divergence in timing of the frontal passage; any clearer skies or delayed cloud arrival could push the observed high toward 18°C, while earlier or thicker cloud would favor the lower side of the range. This leaves the market sensitive to the next 06Z and 12Z model updates ahead of the event.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices a 32% implied probability for Moscow's highest temperature reaching exactly 24°C on May 17, edging out 25°C at 24%, amid tight clustering that reflects genuine forecast uncertainty two days out. Latest ensembles from ECMWF and GFS models, updated May 15, project daily highs near 24–25°C under a warming southerly flow advecting mild air masses, exceeding mid-May climatological norms of 18–20°C by 4–7°C. Key differentiators include late-day showers and overcast skies potentially capping solar heating at 24°C, versus partial clearing allowing brief spikes to 25°C; model spreads capture this, with some runs like Ventusky's ECMWF outlier at 30°C discounted by traders. New runs overnight and Roshydromet advisories will refine guidance before resolution via official station data.
